title: Weight-Loss Medication Changes What People Buy to Wear

source.author: Renan Botelho de Carvalho
source.title: How weight-loss drugs are reshaping wardrobe spending
source.checked_against: Circana's own summary of its 'GLP-1 Unlocked' research (circana.com, found by web search on 2026-11-13) gives the same clothing figure (index 6.4 points above the pre-treatment baseline in the second year) and the same warning that index points are not percentage increases. The other figures were found only in FashionUnited. The day the report came out is left out of the article: FashionUnited says 'Thursday', the search result for Circana's release says November 10. Author and publication date come from the page metadata (the page shows no byline). Extra article requested by Dương on 2026-11-13 to make up for the skipped fashion day 2026-10-30.

figures.text: research by Circana on US households
figures.quote: Circana's latest US household research shows spending in both categories strengthening

figures.text: purchase data from August 2023 to July 2026
figures.quote: Circana's analysis draws on US household receipt-panel purchases from August 2023 to July 2026

figures.text: households with at least one current user who started treatment between 2024 and 2026, compared with households that never used the drugs
figures.quote: households with at least one current user who started treatment between 2024 and 2026

figures.text: year one = first 12 months after treatment began; year two = months 13 to 24
figures.quote: "Year one" refers to the first 12 months after treatment began, while "year two" covers months 13 to 24

figures.text: index tracked against the 12 months before treatment started; index points, not percentage sales increases
figures.quote: These are index-point changes, not percentage sales increases.

figures.text: apparel as a whole: 2.9 points above baseline in year one, 6.4 points in year two
figures.quote: Across apparel as a whole, the spending index was 2.9 points above its pre-treatment baseline in year one

figures.text: swimwear: 15.5 points above baseline in year two, compared with 1.7 in year one
figures.quote: Swimwear's spending index was 15.5 points above its pre-treatment baseline in year two, compared with 1.7

figures.text: outerwear from 10.9 points above baseline to 15 points; sweaters from 6.8 to 14.9 points
figures.quote: Outerwear strengthened from 10.9 points above baseline to 15 points, while sweaters rose from 6.8 to 14.9 points.

figures.text: total footwear: 0.1 points below baseline in year one, 0.2 points below in year two
figures.quote: Total footwear remained close to baseline, at 0.1 points below in year one and 0.2 points below in year two.
Circana's separate September 2026 survey provides evidence of a connection between GLP-1 treatments with clothing purchases.

figures.text: 43% of households with a current user bought clothing or footwear in the previous three months because of the treatment
figures.quote: 43 percent reported buying clothing or footwear in the previous three months because of GLP-1 use.

figures.text: reasons: size changes 28%, updating personal style 18%, new activities 13%
figures.quote: Size changes were the most commonly reported driver, cited by 28 percent ... followed by updating personal style at 18 percent ... and participating in new activities at 13 percent.

figures.text: research does not establish why outerwear and swimwear gain more
figures.quote: Nor does it establish precisely why outerwear and swimwear show stronger gains than

figures.text: advice: look beyond the earliest months of treatment; more responsive size planning
figures.quote: retailers should look beyond the earliest months of treatment when assessing demand.
